requirements.label: 128 Total Credits
requirements.hint: All College of Engineering BSE programs require 128 credit hours.

requirements.label: MATH 115: Calculus I
requirements.hint: Part of the 16 credit CoE mathematics core. AP calculus credit counts here automatically. Honors math sequences also satisfy this per the CoE Bulletin, use the adjust control if your credit posted under a different course number.

requirements.label: MATH 116: Calculus II
requirements.hint: Part of the 16 credit CoE mathematics core. AP calculus credit counts here automatically. Honors math sequences also satisfy this per the CoE Bulletin, use the adjust control if your credit posted under a different course number.

requirements.label: MATH 215 or MATH 216
requirements.hint: Robotics requires one intermediate calculus course, either MATH 215 (multivariable) or MATH 216 (differential equations), per the Robotics degree requirements.

requirements.label: Linear algebra (ROB 101 or equivalent)
requirements.hint: Robotics requires linear algebra. ROB 101, or MATH 214, 217, 417, or 419 satisfies this per the Robotics degree requirements.

requirements.label: Chemistry core
requirements.hint: Either CHEM 130 with the CHEM 125 and 126 labs, or CHEM 210 with the CHEM 211 lab for students who place into organic chemistry. Satisfactory AP chemistry credit also meets this per the CoE Bulletin, use the adjust control if that is your case.

requirements.label: CHEM 130 with labs 125 and 126
requirements.hint: General chemistry with both laboratory courses.

requirements.label: CHEM 210 and CHEM 211
requirements.hint: Organic chemistry path for students who place into CHEM 210. Placement here means no credit is given for CHEM 130.

requirements.label: PHYSICS 140: General Physics I
requirements.hint: CoE physics core. The honors sequence PHYSICS 160 also satisfies this.

requirements.label: PHYSICS 141: Elementary Lab I
requirements.hint: CoE physics core laboratory. The honors lab PHYSICS 161 also satisfies this.

requirements.label: PHYSICS 240: General Physics II
requirements.hint: CoE physics core. The honors sequence PHYSICS 260 also satisfies this.

requirements.label: PHYSICS 241: Elementary Lab II
requirements.hint: CoE physics core laboratory. The honors lab PHYSICS 261 also satisfies this.

requirements.label: ENGR 100: Introduction to Engineering
requirements.hint: A grade of C or better is required. Transfer students may substitute a course meeting the LSA first year writing requirement.

requirements.label: ENGR 101: Introduction to Computers and Programming
requirements.hint: A grade of C or better is required. ENGR 151 is an approved alternative for all CoE programs.

requirements.label: Intellectual Breadth (16 credits)
requirements.hint: 16 credits of liberal arts courses, meaning courses marked HU or SS that are not also marked BS, NS, or QR. ECON 101 and 102 count by explicit exception. Up to 4 credits of approved professional development courses from other U-M schools may also count, use the adjust control to include those.

requirements.label: Humanities minimum (3 credits)
requirements.hint: At least 3 of the 16 Intellectual Breadth credits must be humanities courses. Credit by test cannot be used for this minimum.

requirements.label: Upper level liberal arts minimum (3 credits)
requirements.hint: At least 3 of the 16 Intellectual Breadth credits must be liberal arts courses at the 300 level or higher. One course may satisfy both this and the humanities minimum.

requirements.label: General electives (11 credits)
requirements.hint: Free elective credits that bring the program to 128 total. Any U-M course counts.

requirements.label: Residency (50 credits at U-M Ann Arbor)
requirements.hint: Still building automatic checking for this rule. At least 50 credits must be U-M Ann Arbor coursework, including at least 30 credits of 300 level or higher technical courses offered by the College of Engineering in Ann Arbor.

requirements.label: ROB 204: Introduction to Human-Robot Systems
requirements.hint: Teamwork in robotics. A grade of C or better is required.

requirements.label: Robotics Core (3 courses)
requirements.hint: Choose 3 robotics core courses, each with a grade of C or better. The department lists ROB 310, 311, 320, 330, and 340 as core options, and the degree audit also accepts ROB 314.

requirements.label: Discipline Breadth: Data Structures and Programming
requirements.hint: EECS 280 with a grade of C or better, per the Robotics degree requirements.

requirements.label: Discipline Breadth: Probability, Statistics, and Visualization
requirements.hint: One of IOE 265, EECS 301, or BIOMEDE 241 with a grade of C or better, per the Robotics degree requirements.

requirements.label: Discipline Breadth: Electronics and Circuits
requirements.hint: One of EECS 215, EECS 270, or BIOMEDE 211 with a grade of C or better, per the Robotics degree requirements.

requirements.label: Discipline Breadth: Dynamics and Mechanics
requirements.hint: One of ROB 215, MECHENG 240, or BIOMEDE 231 with a grade of C or better, per the Robotics degree requirements.

requirements.label: Discipline Depth (1 course)
requirements.hint: One approved depth course with a grade of C or better. The department accepts petitions for alternatives not on this list.

requirements.label: TCHNCLCM 350: Technical Communication for Robotics
requirements.hint: Major design communication course, a grade of C or better is required. It is a prerequisite for the capstone.

requirements.label: Robotics Capstone (ROB 450)
requirements.hint: Team based senior design capstone with a grade of C or better. The degree audit names ROB 450, and the department also accepts EECS 467 as the capstone course.

requirements.label: Upper level robotics electives (6 credits)
requirements.hint: At least 2 more graded ROB courses at the 300 level or above for a minimum of 6 credits, each with a C or better, ROB 490 does not count here. The first 12 matching credits are reserved for the Robotics Core row, a fourth core course counts toward this.

requirements.label: Flexible technical electives (to 18 credits total)
requirements.hint: Still building automatic checking for this rule. Technical electives must total 18 credits with a C or better, beyond the upper level robotics minimum the remaining credits come from courses at the 400 level or above in engineering, math, or physics, extra discipline depth or robotics core courses, or program approved 200 and 300 level courses, with at most 4 credits of directed study.

requirements.label: Technical electives: independent study and MDP limit
requirements.hint: Still building automatic checking for this rule. At least 14 of the 18 technical elective credits must come from courses that are not designated as independent studies or multidisciplinary design projects.
